bole.text: Straight cylindrical trunk, light coloured, sometimes pinkish (Spanish Wikipedia); bole free of branches up to 18 m, some basal swellings but no well-developed buttresses (Useful Tropical Plants, src 3). Very old trees sometimes hollow, with shallow spreading roots at the base (src 2).

crown.text: Rounded, dense crown (TTSM src 0, Spanish Wikipedia); 'broadly rounded or elongate' (Useful Tropical Plants).

phenology.flower_colour: pale green to white, turning pink with age (clove-like scent)
phenology.fruit: kidney-shaped drupe (nut) 2.5-3.5 x 1-2 cm, hanging from a curved, fleshy, S-shaped receptacle

bark.colour: brown-grey (grey to black per Spanish Wikipedia); inner bark red or pink
bark.text: Brown-grey bark, scaly or smooth, with leaf scars (TTSM). Spanish Wikipedia: outer bark grey or black, laminar, sometimes with deep vertical fissures; inner bark red or pink with vertical white lines; wounds exude an aromatic resin that turns red or black.

habitat.range: Guatemala/Honduras to Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela and the Guianas; Atlantic and Pacific watersheds.

notes: Leaf habit: Spanish Wikipedia says partly deciduous, leaves yellowing then dropping partly in the dry season and replaced at the start of the rains; English Wikipedia calls it evergreen; TTSM (Fournier, Costa Rica) notes flushes of new foliage in January, then flowers through April (citing Jimenez et al. 1996). No source gives leafless months. Spanish Wikipedia: flowers and fruits Feb-May, fruit ripe Mar-May. Months are Costa Rica/Central America, not Osa-specific. Leaf size: 15-30 x 5-12 cm (en and es Wikipedia description); es Wikipedia habitat section 10-35 x 4-12 cm; leaves clustered at twig ends, obovate, apex rounded, notched or acute. Leaf colour and texture not found. Height: 20-40 m (es Wikipedia), 45 m (TTSM), 48 m (en Wikipedia). dbh max: TTSM 3 m d.b.h.; Useful Tropical Plants up to 200 cm. Habitat: TTSM, often dominant on flood plains and in gallery forests; Useful Tropical Plants, secondary forest, stream sides, sometimes pure stands, young plants need sun and are seldom in mature woodland (basis for 'light-demanding'). The monkey and bat records are Croat's Flora of Barro Colorado (Panama), quoted on the HVAA Symbiota page; the source names them 'white-faced and howler monkeys' and I added the scientific names. Bats eat only the fleshy receptacle and drop the nut (Wikipedia).
